checks: On each fixed fiber the rank-one determinant is ell/L^(d+1). Positive segment weights give the whole image segment irrespective of the sign of nonzero ell. X/L collapses when ell=0 in the stated interval.

For each anchored relation the inverse denominator is the weighted sum of ell(z_j)/L_j, strictly positive. The candidate point is in the target image exactly when its inverse is in K_q. At fixed direction the fractional support root is unique by the common strictly negative slope bound. The linear support inequality on the compact anchored representation polytope reaches its extremum at a vertex.

For a polytopal fiber, averaging the original vertices and then weighting their images by the original coefficients times L gives all image points as convex combinations of image vertices. The homothetic subclass cancels ell directly.

Multiplication by the positive inverse factor yields the stated cap equation with matrix u beta^T minus c a^T. Vanishing is sufficient for the expression itself to be affine. Pure-base caps are preserved by cancellation.

The original strict closed-minor ratios are 4/9,1/3,2/9 below 1/2 and 7/9,5/9 below 1. The transformed endpoint lower midpoint is 1/24 below the middle lower endpoint. The convex-body cap witness misses the midpoint by 1/12. At labels 0,1,2 the proper thresholds have nonzero second difference 2/165.

The positive determinant gives density L^d/ell on the full-dimensional image. Its extrema on the compact fiber yield the exact ratio. The family L=1+X on [0,R] makes it unbounded and c=0 gives ell^(d−1).
Source bd4e19d78aaec9e1 §§1–4 supplies every recorded locator and example. The chart formulas and examples are reproved without importing the older base-only chart calculation.

overlap.comparison: The proof uses positive-denominator segment preservation on a single planar domain. It does not establish the anchored relation across fixed labels, oblique cap failure or tilted density formula.

Its projective orbit uses a denominator depending on the base alone and moves both base and continuous coordinates. Its hull and cap preservation does not imply either preservation or obstruction when labels are held fixed and the denominator varies within a fiber.

readability: The cap condition is sufficient for the expanded expression to be affine. The separate pure-base argument explains why it is not presented as necessary.
